title: Address: a self-contained educational HTML prototype in which an event is a phase address, not a date
description:
Address is a single self-contained HTML page (French user interface; no CDN, no external fonts, no network requests) that illustrates one idea: an event can be identified by its phase address E = (season, shift, machine cycle, block) rather than by its date. Erasing the date leaves the address intact.

Score contract. A synthetic frame of 512 finite values is split into 16 blocks of 32. Each block is scored with S = 0.45·max|x| + 0.35·RMS + 0.20·mean|x| and lights when S ≥ 0.50. The threshold is fixed and never recalibrated; non-finite values are rejected. This is the same block score as the OES32 reference detector in oes-resilience and the classical latch in oes512q-latch. No quantum component enters the score.

Contents. Deterministic seeded synthetic bursts, 16 block scores, five concentric rings, a visible date-erasure action, four preloaded memories (three recur, one does not), an in-page self-test, Node tests that execute the page's single score block, and a forbidden-terms scan in CI.

Limits. Evidence: SYNTHETIC only. Educational prototype; not a field detector, not NASA evidence, not a certified product, not a grant. The preregistered v0.5.0 evaluation of oes-resilience on the public NASA SMAP/MSL dataset did not meet its success criterion; this page makes no claim about real data.
